newsitem.title: UK: Tesco seeks to raise Irish margins.
newsitem.headline: Tesco seeks to raise Irish margins.

text.p: British supermarket chain Tesco Plc said on Friday it hoped to raise operating margins at its newly-acquired Irish businesses to around six percent in three or four years time from 4.7 percent at present.
Finance director David Reid told a news conference Tesco expected to reap buying benefits from the deal, announced earlier on Friday.
Tesco has bought Associated British Food's Plc's Irish retail businesses for 630 million stg.
Reid said sales at the businesses were slightly above average at between 10 stg and 11 stg per square foot.

Tesco chairman Ian MacLaurin said Tesco had not made any decisions on whether to use the Tesco name in Ireland. He noted that Tesco had bought established brand leaders with an inherent value in Ireland.
MacLaurin said he hoped Tesco would be able to launch its storecard -- Clubcard -- within the first year of operation.
Reid said Tesco was unlikely to make further major acquisitions in the wake of the Irish deal.
"There is more likely to be organic growth in Britain and we now have the leading position in Ireland so we wouldn't expect to be adding to these substantial chains," Reid said.
